setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint Stephen** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds St. Stephen played at a perfect pace; The St. Stephen is praised for one clearly beautiful note after another leading into The Eleven [14][17]
- **The Eleven** (2 reviews): Reviewer says The Eleven cooks harder than versions heard before; Reviewer counts this among their favorite versions of The Eleven so far [14][17]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Other One suite raw, heavy and tribal, with intensely focused, dizzying playing; The Cryptical Envelopment into Other One and back sequence is described as mind-bending, psychedelic and furious [7][8]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (1 review): Jerry sings with unusual intensity, with vocals rarely matched elsewhere according to the reviewer [14]
- **Jam** (1 review): Reviewer says the jam following the drums alone justifies downloading this show [13]

## The recordings

- **gd68-10-12.sbd.eD.10909.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 79 min; rated 4.88/5 by 81 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears the soundboard as crystal clean, revealing detail in the music; Clear enough to hear a percussive scratching sound, perhaps a wood block, during Jerry's vocals; Reviewer describes the sound quality as warm and pleasantly fuzzy [8][9][17]
- **gd1968-10-12.139745.sbd.miller.Glassberg.flac1644**: soundboard; 10 songs; 91 min; rated 5/5 by 7 [4]
- **gd1968-10-12.sbd.miller.86759.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 79 min; rated 4.79/5 by 48 [2]
- **gd1968-10-12.sbd.gans.miller.owen.9385.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 79 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [3]

## Around the show

- Audience can be heard groaning in stunned reaction between the band's intense bursts of playing [8]
- Reviewer recounts that Jimi Hendrix was playing nearby at Winterland and wanted to jam with the Dead [10]
- Reportedly the Dead arranged a ferry boat for an all-night jam the previous night, but Hendrix didn't appear [10]
- Reportedly Hendrix turned up at the Avalon on this night seeking another chance to play with the band [10]
- On reviewer's older tape, a rowdy crowd is told by Jerry to cool it, as the band would play till they dropped [11]
- Other artists listed for the date are Lee Michaels, Linn County and Mance Lipscomb [4]
- Reviewer considers it the best 1968 show heard so far [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-10-12.sbd.eD.10909.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Gans and Frisco; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer's early trade tape of this show was mislabeled as 10-31-68; This version lacks the stage banter that appears on the reviewer's older tape of the show [9][11]
- **gd1968-10-12.139745.sbd.miller.Glassberg.flac1644**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SHNID #115593 > Adobe Audition 3.0 > Flac16 [4]. Also: Glassberg's reel, via CD-R from Chuck Reynolds, supplies the pre-Dark Star banter and the Morning Dew; transfer details unknown [4]
- **gd1968-10-12.sbd.miller.86759.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]
- **gd1968-10-12.sbd.gans.miller.owen.9385.shnf**: transferred by David Gans; source: MSR> DAT> Sonic Solutions> CD [3]
